rationale:
Security-posture lens on 8eaeb05e vs ae45fd7a. Read ADR-0042 (render+derivation provenance) in full and traced its five-consumer taxonomy against every NEW surface this branch adds: bd stderr capture/rendering (bead 9's wrapBDError/capStderrLines/bdRenderedError), porcelain -z entanglement parsing (bead 7's parsePorcelainZ/dirtyEntry/renderDirtyEntry/IgnoredDirtNotice), bead-title/ID rendering across next.go/select.go/beads.go/guard.go, and the Mindspec-Stage trailer + write-ahead marker protocol (bead 6). Ran `go build ./...` (clean) and `go test ./internal/lint/... -short -v` (all ratchet enforcers green, including the real go/ast wrapper-agnostic argv scanner TestArgvIDOperandGated) — the mechanical completeness claim in ADR-0042 §5/§8 is not just documented, it is a passing build-time test today. Verified by direct source read, not just table prose: FileExistsAtRef (ref+path both rejectOptionLike-gated before cat-file composition), Toplevel/ResetIndexOnlyMixed (zero dynamic operands), UpdateRefCAS/AdvanceBranchExpectedOld/MaterializeStageCommit/ChangedFilesTree (all typed operands rejectOptionLike-gated exactly as their table notes claim), RevParseRef (gates its ref argument, so ReadMaterializationMarker/PublishMaterializationMarker inherit that gate transitively). The Mindspec-Stage trailer forgery path is sound: ReadStageTrailer treats ANY duplicate trailer line (forged via a crafted --commit-msg or otherwise) as ambiguous-and-absent regardless of whether the two lines agree, so an operator cannot smuggle a fake single trailer through the appended real one; materializationSubject's --commit-msg text only ever reaches argv as -m's VALUE, never a positional ref/tree operand, so it cannot be parsed as a git option. Rendering discipline is applied consistently and with real judgment, not cargo-culted: DirtyTreeFailure escapes each porcelain entry per-line (termsafe.Escape correctly whole-string-quotes on ANY embedded control byte including a raw newline from a hostile filename, verified against internal/termsafe's own test table), while IgnoredDirtNotice deliberately uses unconditional strconv.Quote instead because it joins multiple entries on one comma-separated line and needs self-delimiting quoting to stop a hostile ', '-containing filename from forging a fake boundary between two different paths — and the code says so in a comment. select.go/beads.go/next.go consistently route ID-typed positions through idrender.Bead/idrender.Spec and free-text through termsafe.Escape, including one place (select.go SelectWorkByName's ambiguous/not-found errors) where the code comment cites its OWN round-1 panel finding that a prior raw %s was fixed to termsafe.Escape(name) — i.e. this exact class of self-audit has already caught and fixed a real gap once. bdcli.go's capStderrLines bounds by line count only (20 lines), not bytes, but this is not a live gap: RunBD/tracedOutput use cmd.Output() with Stderr left nil, so Go's stdlib already caps captured stderr at 64KB via the internal prefixSuffixSaver before capStderrLines ever sees it — a hostile single-line-no-newline bd stderr is bounded by the runtime, not just by this app-level cap.

Why REQUEST_CHANGES: one argv-audit-table entry makes a false claim about the code it describes, in the exact file (internal/gitutil/materialize.go) whose sibling entries this SAME final review's bead-6 per-bead panel already caught doing this twice (R2's round-1 and round-2 verdicts, spec-128-bead6/R2-round-{1,2}.json, both flagged 'the count-exact ratchet cannot catch prose drift, which is exactly why the note must be corrected by hand'). internal/lint/ratchet_argv_table_test.go's entry for ClearMaterializationMarker (Class: opClassRejectOptionLikeGated) asserts 'the SAME ref-composition-then-RejectOptionLike-gating shape as UpdateRefCAS's entry above'. It is not: I read ClearMaterializationMarker (internal/gitutil/materialize.go:356-372) line by line and it contains ZERO calls to rejectOptionLike, on either the composed ref or on expectedOID, unlike UpdateRefCAS (materialize.go:254-272) which explicitly gates ref, newSHA, and old before building argv. expectedOID is interpolated directly into `git update-ref -d <ref> <expectedOID>`'s argv with no runtime guard at all. This is not exploitable today because every real caller (internal/executor.MindspecExecutor.ClearStageMarker's two internal/complete.go sites and materialize.go's own two discriminator sites) passes an OID that was itself produced by git rev-parse/RevParseRef moments earlier — a 40-char lowercase-hex SHA can never start with '-', so it is safe by PROVENANCE. But ADR-0042 §1 explicitly forbids exactly this reasoning pattern for id-typed operands ('no id operand is trusted by PROVENANCE anywhere'), and the lint schema's own closed enum already has the honest class for this situation — opClassRevParseSHA ('git SHAs / rev-parse'd refs, hex-validated by git itself') — which is what MaterializeStageCommit's/ChangedFilesTree's sibling entries correctly use for their SHA-shaped operands elsewhere in this same table. The fix is cheap and strictly improves the branch either way: either (a) reclassify the entry to opClassRevParseSHA with an accurate note naming the real hex-provenance guarantee, or (b) actually add rejectOptionLike(expectedOID) inside ClearMaterializationMarker (mirroring UpdateRefCAS), which is strictly better — it converts an implicit, provenance-only assumption into a real runtime gate that would catch a future caller who starts forwarding non-SHA text, and makes the table's existing claim true instead of false. Given this exact file's own history in this branch (two rounds of the SAME class of prose-drift finding on adjacent table entries), a reviewer or future maintainer who trusts this note as ground truth is being told there is a runtime guard where none exists.
concrete_changes_required: internal/lint/ratchet_argv_table_test.go: fix the ClearMaterializationMarker entry (key "internal/gitutil/materialize.go ClearMaterializationMarker exec-git execCommand"). It currently claims 'the SAME ref-composition-then-RejectOptionLike-gating shape as UpdateRefCAS's entry above' but internal/gitutil/materialize.go:356-372's ClearMaterializationMarker calls execCommand directly and never calls rejectOptionLike on either the composed ref or expectedOID (unlike UpdateRefCAS, which gates all three of its operands). Preferred fix: add `if err := rejectOptionLike(expectedOID); err != nil { return err }` (and, for symmetry with the sibling functions in this file, gate the composed ref too) at the top of ClearMaterializationMarker so the code actually matches the existing claim — this also closes the gap where a future caller could forward non-SHA text into this argv unguarded. If the team prefers not to touch the function, the minimum acceptable alternative is reclassifying the table entry to Class: opClassRevParseSHA with a note stating the real guarantee: expectedOID is always the return value of a prior git rev-parse (RevParseRef/ReadMaterializationMarker), never attacker-supplied text, so it cannot be option-like by construction of hex-SHA output — but this is the weaker fix since it documents a provenance-trust argument ADR-0042 §1 otherwise forbids for id-shaped operands.

findings.title: ClearMaterializationMarker's argv-audit-table entry claims a RejectOptionLike gate that does not exist in the function
findings.detail: internal/lint/ratchet_argv_table_test.go's ClearMaterializationMarker entry (Class: opClassRejectOptionLikeGated) says the call carries 'the SAME ref-composition-then-RejectOptionLike-gating shape as UpdateRefCAS's entry above'. The actual function (internal/gitutil/materialize.go:356-372) builds `git update-ref -d <ref> <expectedOID>` argv via execCommand directly, with no rejectOptionLike call anywhere in its body -- unlike every sibling marker function in the same file (RevParseRef, UpdateRefCAS, AdvanceBranchExpectedOld, MaterializeStageCommit, ChangedFilesTree), which all gate their dynamic operands before use. Not exploitable today: every real call site passes a git-computed hex SHA (RevParseRef/ReadMaterializationMarker output), which can never start with '-'. But this is exactly the id-operand provenance-trust reasoning ADR-0042 SS1 forbids ('no id operand is trusted by PROVENANCE anywhere'), the lint schema has no AST-level check that verifies opClassRejectOptionLikeGated entries actually contain a rejectOptionLike call (checkArgvEntrySchema only validates the Class name against a closed enum, never cross-references the source), and this SAME table in this SAME bead already had two rounds of near-identical prose-drift findings during bead 6's own panel (spec-128-bead6/R2-round-1.json and R2-round-2.json, both about MaterializeStageCommit's note going stale after a mid-round code change) -- this is a recurring, not hypothetical, failure mode for this specific file.

findings.title: bd stderr line-count cap has no independent byte bound, but is backstopped by Go's stdlib
findings.detail: internal/bead/bdcli.go's capStderrLines bounds captured bd stderr to bdStderrExcerptLineCap=20 LINES, not bytes -- a single unbroken line with no newline would pass through uncapped by this function alone. Verified this is not a live gap: tracedOutput/RunBD call cmd.Output() with cmd.Stderr left nil, so exec.ExitError.Stderr is already bounded to Go's stdlib prefixSuffixSaver limit (32KB head + 32KB tail, 64KB total) before capStderrLines ever runs. No change required; noting for the record since the doc comment's stated purpose ('bound a pathological or hostile bd emitting unbounded stderr') is achieved by composition with the stdlib default rather than by this function alone, which is worth knowing if RunBD's cmd construction is ever changed to set an explicit unbounded Stderr writer.

findings.title: Verified: porcelain -z rename/entanglement handling and its rendering are correctly hardened
findings.detail: parsePorcelainZ (internal/next/guard.go) correctly relies on NUL-delimited fields to avoid the newline-form's ' -> ' ambiguity for renamed paths containing that literal substring; entryIntersectsEntangleable checks both Path and OrigPath for rename/copy entries per the round-1 panel's own G3/G6 fix. renderDirtyEntry's output (including a possible embedded raw newline from a hostile filename byte, which -z output does not escape) is safely handled downstream: DirtyTreeFailure calls termsafe.Escape on the whole per-entry string, and termsafe.Escape correctly detects ANY non-printable-ASCII byte anywhere in the string (including an embedded \n) and quotes the ENTIRE string via strconv.Quote rather than only the offending byte -- confirmed against internal/termsafe's own test table (TestTermsafeEscape_SafeSetQuoteAndNoOp's 'newline: line1\nline2' case). IgnoredDirtNotice's separate choice of unconditional strconv.Quote (rather than termsafe.Escape) for its comma-joined multi-entry line is deliberately reasoned in-code and correct for the different risk it defends against (entry-boundary forging via a literal ', ' inside a filename).
findings.location: internal/next/guard.go (parsePorcelainZ, entryIntersectsEntangleable, renderDirtyEntry, DirtyTreeFailure, IgnoredDirtNotice); internal/termsafe/termsafe.go
